questions.question: The following is an antibiotic

__
 
• **Streptomycin:**

 
 
• Streptomycin is an **aminoglycoside antibiotic **indicated to treat **multi-drug resistant mycobacterium tuberculosis** and various non-tuberculosis infections. 
 
• It is derived from **Streptomyces griseus**, which was the first aminoglycoside to be discovered and used in practice in the** 1940s.**

• Tuberculosis is **curable and preventable**.
 
• TB is spread from person to person through the air.

• The bacteria that cause tuberculosis (TB) can develop** resistance to the antimicrobial drugs** used to cure the disease.

questions.question: Where does protein synthesis occur in the cell?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Ribosomes.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes** are macromolecular machines, found within all living cells, which perform biological protein synthesis.
 
• Ribosomes consist of two major components: the small and large ribosomal subunits. Each sub-unit consists of one or more ribosomal RNA (rRNA) molecules and many ribosomal proteins (RPs or r-proteins).
 
• **Ribosomes** were first observed in the mid-1950s by Romanian-American cell biologist George Emil Palade, using an electron microscope, as dense particles or granules. The term '**ribosome**' was proposed by scientist Richard B. Roberts at the end of the 1950s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Golgi apparatus, also known as the Golgi complex, Golgi body, or simply the Golgi, is an organelle found in most eukaryotic cells. Part of the endomembrane system in the cytoplasm, it packages proteins into membrane-bound vesicles inside the cell before the vesicles are sent to their destination.
 
• The **mitochondrion** is a double membrane-bound organelle found in most eukaryotic organisms. Some cells in some multicellular organisms lack **mitochondria.**
 
• **Centrosomes** are organelles that serve as the main microtubule-organizing centres for animal cells. **Centrosomes** are made up of two, barrel-shaped clusters of microtubules called '**centrioles**'.

questions.question: Identify an organelle found both in eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes** are the only organelles found in both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.
 
• They are responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• Ribosomes can be found floating freely within the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotic cells.
 
• In prokaryotic cells, ribosomes are smaller (70S) compared to those in eukaryotic cells (80S).
 
• Despite the size difference, the fundamental function of ribosomes remains the same across both cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prokaryotic cells** do not have membrane-bound organelles, which distinguishes them from eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Eukaryotic cells** contain various membrane-bound organelles, including the nucleus, mitochondria, and lysosomes, which are absent in prokaryotic cells.
 
• The presence of ribosomes in both cell types highlights their essential role in the fundamental process of protein synthesis.
 
• The differences in ribosome size between prokaryotes and eukaryotes are due to variations in their ribosomal RNA and protein content.

questions.question: Which of the following Cell organelle is responsible for Aerobic respiration ?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Mitochondria**

__
 
• Mitochondria are membrane-bound organelles found in the cytoplasm of all eukaryotic cells.
 
• They produce **adenosine triphosphate (ATP),** the cell's primary energy molecule.
 
• Mitochondria are known as the cell's **powerhouses **because they create **energy-rich compounds**.
 
• It's a sausage-shaped organelle with two membranes.
 
• Mitochondria have circular DNA, RNA molecules, ribosomes (from the 1970s), and a few additional molecules that aid protein synthesis.
 
• The lumen is divided into two different aqueous compartments by the double membranes.
 
• The inner compartment is referred to as the **matrix**, and it is folded into **cristae**, while the outside membrane forms a **continuous **barrier with the cytoplasm.
 
• They are usually round or oval in shape and come in a variety of sizes.

 ​

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• Mitochondria are called the powerhouse of the cell because it produces ATP, which is the energy-giving molecule.
 
• The ATP is released in the process of **aerobic respiration** within the mitochondria, in the presence of oxygen. 
 
• Hence, the correct answer to this question is - **Mitochondria**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__**Functions:**__

 
• The primary purpose of mitochondria is to produce energy via the oxidative phosphorylation process. Mitochondria are the cell's aerobic respiration sites, producing energy in the form of ATP in the presence of oxygen. Glucose, is transformed into adenosine triphosphate (ATP).
 
• Controls the cell's metabolic activities.
 
• Encourages the formation of new cells and the multiplication of existing ones.
 
• Aids in the detoxification of ammonia in liver cells.
 
• Apoptosis (programmed cell death) is a process through which cells die.
 
• It is responsible for the formation of some blood components as well as hormones such as testosterone and estrogen.
 
• Assists in maintaining a sufficient calcium ion concentration inside the cell compartments.
 
• It also plays a role in cellular differentiation, cell signaling, cell senescence, cell cycle control, and cell proliferation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about cells is correct?

options.text: Mitochondria is a jelly-like substance present between the cell membrane and nucleus
Mitochondria, golgi bodies, ribosomes, etc are present in the nuclear membrane
Nuclear membrane surrounding the nucleus is porous allowing the movement of materials
Nuclear membrane is made up of thread-like structures called chromosomes

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is__** Nuclear membrane surrounding the nucleus is porous allowing the movement of materials.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• **Mitochondria is a jelly-like substance present between the cell membrane and nucleus:** This **statement is incorrect.** Mitochondria are organelles found in eukaryotic cells and are not jelly-like substances. They are double-membraned organelles responsible for energy production through cellular respiration. They are not located between the cell membrane and the nucleus; instead, they are dispersed throughout the cytoplasm of the cell.
 
• **Mitochondria, Golgi bodies, ribosomes, etc. are present in the nuclear membrane: **This **statement is incorrect.** Mitochondria, Golgi bodies, and ribosomes are not present in the nuclear membrane. Mitochondria, as mentioned earlier, are separate organelles in the cytoplasm. Golgi bodies are organelles involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins, and they are also found in the cytoplasm. Ribosomes, which are responsible for protein synthesis, can be found in the cytoplasm (free ribosomes) or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum (bound ribosomes). None of these organelles are present within the nuclear membrane.
 
• **The nuclear membrane surrounding the nucleus is porous, allowing the movement of materials:** This** statement is correct.** The nuclear membrane, also known as the nuclear envelope, is a double-membrane structure that surrounds the nucleus in eukaryotic cells. It is porous and contains nuclear pores, which allow for the controlled movement of materials between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. This enables the transport of molecules like RNA and proteins into and out of the nucleus, facilitating various cellular processes, including gene expression and protein synthesis.** The types of materials that move through the nuclear pores include RNA molecules, proteins, ribosomal subunits, and other smaller molecules and ions, ensuring proper cellular function and gene expression.**
 
• **The nuclear membrane is made up of thread-like structures called chromosomes: **This** statement is incorrect.** The nuclear membrane is not made up of chromosomes. Chromosomes are thread-like structures made up of DNA and proteins found inside the nucleus. They contain the genetic information of the cell. The nuclear membrane, on the other hand, is a separate cellular structure that encloses the nucleus and separates it from the cytoplasm.

questions.question: Chromosomes are located in the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chromosomes are **thread-like structures** located **inside the nucleus of animal and plant cells**.
 
• Each chromosome is **made of protein and a single molecule of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA)**.
 
• Passed from parents to offspring, DNA contains the specific instructions that make each type of living creature unique.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Chromosomes**

 
 
• Chromosomes are divided into **two parts (p and q arms)** with a constriction point called a centromere in the middle. 
 
• **Metacentric **– centromere is in **middle**, meaning p and q arms are of comparable length (e.g. chromosomes 1, 3, 16, 19, 20).
 
• **Submetacentric **– centromere** off-centre**, leading to shorter p arm relative to q arm (e.g. chromosomes 2, 4 – 12, 17, 18, X).
 
• **Acrocentric **– centromere severely **off-set from the centre**, leading to much shorter p arm (e.g. chromosomes 13 – 15, 21, 22, Y).
 
• **Telocentric** – centromere found at **end of a chromosome**, meaning no p arm exists (chromosome not found in humans).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In humans, each cell normally contains **23 pairs of chromosomes, for a total of 46**.
 
• **Twenty-two of these pairs, called autosomes**, look the same in both males and females.
 
• The **23rd pair, the sex chromosomes**, differ between males and females.
 
• Females have **two copies of the X chromosome**, while males** have one X and one Y chromosome**.

questions.question: Which of the following organelles shows similarity to a prokaryotic cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Both chloroplast and mitochondria**

Concept:

Theory of endosymbiosis:-

 
• Symbiotic relationship, where one organism lives inside the other, is known as **endosymbiosis. **
 
• The theory proposed that mitochondria and chloroplasts evolved from **engulfed prokaryotes.**
 
• A **large anaerobic bacteria **engulfed an **aerobic prokaryote**, which then formed an **endosymbiotic relationship **with the host, gradually developing into a mitochondrion.
 
• It is believed that **chloroplasts** originated from a **cyanobacterial endosymbiont.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e18e9f1fa1dc54744ced2652aee194188080e021a1f2698fa9b073a92801187c.png] 

Explanation:

Similarities between **Prokaryotic cells, Mitochondria, and Chloroplast:**

 
• Mitochondria and chloroplast are of the **same size as prokaryotic cells.**
 
• Mitochondria and prokaryotic cells both have their own **circular DNA.**

questions.question: _________ is a part of DNA, which provides information for a protein.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gene**__.

__
 
• **Gene **____**is a part of DNA, which provides information for a protein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Genes** are **functional units** of heredity as they are made of DNA. The chromosome is made of **DNA containing many genes.**

 
 
• Every gene comprises a particular set of instructions for a particular function or **protein-coding**. Speaking in usual terms, genes are responsible for heredity.
 
• There are about** 30000 genes **in each cell of the** human body**. **DNA present** in the gene comprises only **2 percent of the genome.**
 
• Many studies have been made on the same that found the location of nearly **13000 genes** on **each of the chromosomes**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **William Bateson** introduced the term **genetics** in the year **1905**.

 
 
• **Wilhelm Johannes** was the first one who coined the term **GENE** in **1909**.
 
• He was a Danish botanist.
 
• He named it **Gene** to symbolize hereditary.
